# Validation

Generated from INA-sim 0.3.0. Reproduce with `ina-sim validate`.

An anchor is only worth having if it is independent of the numbers it tests. Checking a polynomial against itself proves nothing, so each anchor below is a claim made in the source's prose, an ordering the source asserts, a textbook regime the model must land in, or a calibration check that published measurements really do fall inside the uncertainty band this tool advertises.

## What each anchor is testing

### `kaolinite_rate_at_239k`

Murray et al. (2011), Sect. 7, comparing their kaolinite rate with Niedermeier et al. (2010): "They find a J value of 10^7 cm-2 s-1 at 239 K, whereas we report a value of ~10^5 cm-2 s-1 at the same temperature." The prose value is independent of Eq. (24)'s coefficients, so reproducing it tests the transcription.

### `mineral_activity_ordering`

Harrison et al. (2019), Sect. 5.1: "there is a general trend in that plagioclase feldspars are the least active of the four mineral groups and K-feldspar is the most active. Both albite and quartz show similar, intermediate, activities." All four fits share the BET area basis, so they are directly comparable.

*Caveat:* Albite and quartz are listed in the order the paper's figure shows them; the paper calls their activities "similar", and the separation this fit produces (0.8-1.4 decades) is within the quoted sigma of 0.7-0.8, so the ordering between those two is checked but is not evidence of a real gap.

### `homogeneous_freezing_regime`

Micrometre-sized pure water droplets freeze homogeneously in the -35 to -38 C range. This is an end-to-end check: it exercises the rate coefficient, the unit conversions and the cooling-ramp integration together, and it fails loudly if any of them is wrong by a factor of ten.

### `agi_band_covers_measurements`

The AgI fit advertises a 1-sigma band of 1.82 decades. For that claim to be honest, roughly the Gaussian fraction of the underlying measurements must fall inside it. Requiring at least 60 percent coverage at 1 sigma detects both an understated band and a fit that has drifted off the data.

### `agi_band_covers_measurements_2sigma`

At 2 sigma essentially every measurement must be inside the band. If it is not, the quoted uncertainty is too small and every downstream number is overconfident.
